title: Land a job only on the branch it was dispatched from
summary: Landing (`land::plan`, called from run/close.rs at ~228 and ~484) only checks the job's base is an ancestor of HEAD, so a job lands on whatever branch is checked out at finish. The change records the dispatch branch and makes the job stale (or blocked on retry) with a clear reason when the current branch differs. The audience is the Athena user who switches branches while jobs run.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for the branch rule; cargo test and clippy clean.
Behavior criteria are checked by running cargo test.
The rule goes in land::plan, so both landing paths get it.
The land.rs header and CHANGELOG state the rule for an outside reader.
Criteria check that a job does not land on the wrong branch, not that wiring exists.
One focused change to the landing decision.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: entry points are `plan` in crates/athena-core/src/land.rs (checks `is_ancestor(base, head)`, then classification, then fingerprint) and its two callers in crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs (~228 first landing, ~484 retry after blocked); `current_branch()` is in crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs:344. The new branch check runs first in `plan`, before the ancestor check. `Outcome.branch` (crates/athena-data/src/records.rs:872) records the branch at finish, not at dispatch, so the dispatch branch must come from the job's dispatch-time state or context. Preferred: reuse an existing dispatch-time field and leave records.rs unchanged. If a new optional field is added to a record in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs, it must be accepted by `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord` there (the records validation, with `deny_unknown_fields`), and covered by that file's existing round-trip tests. The behavior is measured directly: by running a real land through `plan` and the close.rs paths on a git fixture with two branches and checking the branch tip and the outcome state.
Detached HEAD at dispatch or at finish: treat a differing or absent branch as stale, with a reason saying so.
Jobs dispatched before this change have no recorded dispatch branch; they keep the old behavior (no branch check) rather than going stale.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`. A new test dispatches a job on branch A, switches to branch B (which contains the base commit), finishes the job, and shows that B's tip is unchanged and the outcome is stale (or blocked) with a reason naming the dispatch branch.
Run `cargo test`. A test shows a job still lands as a fast-forward when the checked-out branch at finish is the dispatch branch, including the records-only-changes replay case.
Run `cargo test`. A test shows the retry-after-blocked landing path (close.rs ~484) also refuses when the current branch differs from the dispatch branch.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean, and the existing land and landing tests in crates/athena-core still pass.
The header comment of crates/athena-core/src/land.rs states the rule that the current branch must equal the dispatch branch, alongside the existing ancestor rule.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry stating that jobs now land only on the branch they were dispatched from.
Run `cargo test`. If a record field is added, the round-trip tests for `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord` in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs pass with it and with records that lack it.
This change refuses more landings, and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 5% of newly refused readings.

out_of_scope: Changing how jobs are dispatched or read.
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow files.
Auto-switching branches or auto-redispatching stale jobs.
departures: Slightly longer than the reference because dispatch-branch storage and two landing paths need tests.
hard_reason: Changes the landing rule in land::plan and the close pipeline, which can refuse or hold a job from landing.
